question: Does ClientInfo field 16 (triggerApplicationId), the only editor-derived request field Android sets that the native client omitted, change advanced-mode behavior?
method: Same synthetic utterances, one session per arm, no retries; value = package name of the owned test editor (org.rambpc.publicvoiceprobe), no other identity used.
conclusion: Field 16 alone does not trigger COMPOSE/RAMBLE behavior for these utterances; the option is kept (Android parity, off by default).
limits: Two utterances, one session each; not proof that no profile triggers composition.
